page: Amazon Web Services r7i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 16 virtual CPUs derived from 8 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The compute subsystem includes 105 MB of shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance delivers a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps, while dedicated local disk storage and GPU hardware are absent, requiring reliance on remote network-attached block storage.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid single-thread execution efficiency, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 2141.0 alongside elevated single-threaded gzip compression at 33.78 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.9 GB/sec. Multithreaded workloads and overall system capacity align with the mid-tier profile for this core count, scoring 12699.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 26176.98 on PassMark CPU. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth registers at 100.58 GB/sec for reads and 77.32 GB/sec for writes. In application-level benchmarks, the configuration achieves 21.24 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and supports small-model (135M) LLM text generation at 333.12 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7i.4xlarge delivers a high density of modern DDR5 memory per compute core, maximizing utilization for environments limited by RAM rather than raw processing speed. However, workloads requiring intensive local disk I/O face throughput constraints over network storage interfaces. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, key-value caches like Redis, mid-sized relational database management systems, big data processing, and large-scale ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8488C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. Supported by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it integrates 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside 105 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance provisions a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated local storage, and excludes GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight upper-quartile single-threaded performance in Geekbench and compression tasks, paired with consistent median multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth. It maintains an efficient hardware balance for memory-constrained workloads such as Redis deployments, in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, and data transformation pipelines.
